title: Shift Codebook — Snap Notes for Handoff
body:
Purpose:
Quick personal scratchpad for a +1 shift handoff. Not a formal runbook — use as a compact context dump for the next person. Add anything you do during the shift and mark items under FOLLOWUP.

Top-of-shift summary:
- Observability: No active P0s. Alert volume normal (steady ~12 alerts/hr), but pay attention to increased 5xx on /v1/generate from eu-west-1 during bursts.
- Deploys: Canary rollout for optimize-service stopped at 40% at 03:20 UTC due to slow startup on quantized model. Patch in progress (PR #1108).
- Capacity: Dedicated pool "dedicated-gpu-a" at 78% (expected), autoscaler healthy.

Quick checks to run on takeover (commands):
- Check alert backlog: gcloud logging read "resource.type=cloud_run_revision AND severity>=ERROR" --limit 50
- Service health: kubectl get pods -n inference-prod -o wide | grep serve-runtime
- Rolling restarts if memory leak suspected: kubectl rollout restart deployment/serve-runtime -n inference-prod
- Cache status: redis-cli -h redis-prod.info TTL prompt_cache:* | wc -l (look for many expired entries)

Escalation ladder (short):
1) On-call SRE (you) — triage and attempt quick mitigation
2) Senior SRE (Jonas) — if error rate > 5% for > 20m or persistent OOMs
3) Platform Eng (Rina) — networking/hypervisor hardware issues or cross-region routing faults
4) PagerDuty escalation to on-call manager if incident is P0 > 60m or data breach suspicion

Common incidents and quick mitigations (temp fixes):
- Symptom: sudden spike in inference tail latency (P95 > 2s)
  Temp fix: switch routing to lower-cost model variant with same topology -> CLI: redwood route set --service serve-runtime --model llama-70b-8bit --priority low-latency (this reduces accuracy but restores tail).
  Follow-up: file a perf regression ticket with traces and sample prompts.

- Symptom: memory OOMs on worker pods after recent quantization change
  Temp fix: scale replicas up by +2: kubectl scale deployment/serve-runtime --replicas=<current+2> -n inference-prod. If OOM persists, roll back to previous image tag: kubectl set image deployment/serve-runtime serve-runtime=registry/redwood/serve-runtime:2024-09-19 -n inference-prod
  Note: Rolling back will clear the new caching behavior; coordinate with product if rollback needed.

- Symptom: prefix cache returning stale completions (observed twice this week)
  Temp fix: flush affected keyspace: redis-cli -h redis-prod.info EVAL "return redis.call('del', unpack(redis.call('keys', ARGV[1])))" 0 "prefix_cache:user:*"
  Risk: short downtime for those cached prefixes — warn support.

Monitoring dashboards to glance at (Quick links in my head):
- console.redwood/dashboard/latency-overview (P95 & error ratio)
- console.redwood/dashboard/kv-cache-hit-ratio (watch for dips < 60%)
- grafana/redwood/serve-runtime (heap/GC, open fds)

Unresolved / rough TODOs (FOLLOWUP):
- Investigate slow canary startups: suspect the init container pulling quantized model artifacts; possible S3 throttling. ACTION: check s3 access patterns + upload latency around 03:00-04:00 UTC. (Assigned to Jonas in JIRA-4321.)
- Consolidate alert rules that fire together: alert storm from memory/cpu + queue length. Propose an umbrella alert that de-duplicates.
- Add a one-button runbook for prefix-cache flush with safeguards (confirm and ttl snapshot).

Incident notes (recent):
- 2024-10-01 02:55 UTC: transient P1 — eu-west-1 API 5xx spike for 18m. Cause: slow kernel update rolled to nocluster image on one AZ -> autoscaler spiked; mitigated by draining that node and restarting scaled pods.
- Actions taken: cordon + drain node-az3-eu; restarted 3 pods; increased autoscaler min for the time window.

Cheat commands I keep using (copy to your clipboard):
- kubectl -n inference-prod describe pod <pod-name> | grep -A5 Events\- journalctl -u rserve --since "10m" --no-pager\- s3api list-objects --bucket redwood-models --prefix quantized/llama-70b/ --query "length(Contents[])"

Communication templates (short):
- Slack incident start: "Heads up: seeing elevated 5xx on /v1/generate in eu-west-1 starting ~02:45 UTC. Triage in progress, linking traces and current mitigation steps."
- Slack update: "Mitigation applied: routing temporarily switched to llama-70b-8bit for low latency. Will revert when canary is healthy. ETA 30-45m."

Notes to self and reminders:
- If you restart the optimizer service, watch the cold-start tokenization spike — I usually mute alerts for 5 minutes using the console.
- Keep an eye on error messages mentioning "kvcache corruption" — escalate to Rina immediately; we suspect a serialization mismatch after the quantize change.
- Document exact model tags and container image IDs if you roll back — this saves debugging later.

Personal on-shift checklist (checkboxes for me):
- [ ] Read active alerts and silence noisy duplicates
- [ ] Confirm canary topology change status
- [ ] Notify support if cache flush performed
- [ ] Add notes to incident JIRA if any manual workaround used

Closing handoff note to next person:
If I'm leaving and the canary is still at 40%: leave it alone unless error rate > 3% for more than 15m. If you do change routing/model choices, paste the command and the before/after metrics into the handoff. I pinned the last grafana snapshot to the incident JIRA. Good luck and ping me on slack if anything strange shows up — I'm likely offline after 11:30 UTC.

-- Aisha
